# openssl — 2008 high-value CVEs (CVSS>=7, CISA KEV, Exploit-DB, or SSVC exploitation active/poc)

Full records for all 8 openssl CVEs of 2008 are in `data/cve/vendors/openssl/2008.jsonl`.

### CVE-2008-0166
- Assigner: mitre | Published: 2008-05-13 | Updated: 2024-08-07 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 5622: OpenSSL 0.9.8c-1 < 0.9.8g-9 (Debian and Derivatives) - Predictable PRNG Brute Force SSH (remote/linux, 2008-05-15, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 5720: OpenSSL 0.9.8c-1 < 0.9.8g-9 (Debian and Derivatives) - Predictable PRNG Brute Force SSH (remote/linux, 2008-06-01, verified=1)
- Exploit-DB 5632: OpenSSL 0.9.8c-1 < 0.9.8g-9 (Debian and Derivatives) - Predictable PRNG Brute Force SSH (Ruby) (remote/linux, 2008-05-16, verified=1)

OpenSSL 0.9.8c-1 up to versions before 0.9.8g-9 on Debian-based operating systems uses a random number generator that generates predictable numbers, which makes it easier for remote attackers to conduct brute force guessing attacks against cryptographic keys.
